10.description: You've reached 10 weeks, and your little one is now officially a fetus! This is a major milestone as all their essential organs have formed. Many people find their early pregnancy symptoms start to ease up around now.
10.mom_tip: If nausea is fading, try reintroducing healthy proteins.

11.description: Your baby is about the size of a fig, and tiny fingernails are starting to form. They're already moving around, but you probably won't feel it for a few more weeks.
11.mom_tip: Hydration is key—try coconut water if plain water is boring.

12.description: You've reached the end of the first trimester! Your baby's reflexes are developing, and they can now open and close their hands and curl their toes.
12.mom_tip: Celebrate finishing the first trimester with some self-care!

13.description: Welcome to the second trimester! Many people find their energy levels start to return and morning sickness subsides. Your baby's vocal cords are now developing.
13.mom_tip: Use that returning energy for gentle walks or prenatal yoga.

14.description: Your baby is starting to grow fine hair, called lanugo, all over their body, which helps keep them warm. They can also make facial expressions now, like squinting and frowning.
14.mom_tip: Constipation is common now; increase fiber intake.

15.description: Your baby can now sense light. If you were to shine a flashlight on your belly, they might move away from the beam. Their taste buds are also forming.
15.mom_tip: Sleeping on your side is safer now than on your back.

16.description: Your baby's sensory development is kicking into high gear. They can now make sucking motions with their mouth, and their tiny ears are in their final position.
16.mom_tip: Back pain starting? Look into a pregnancy pillow.

17.description: The skeleton is starting to harden from soft cartilage to bone. You might start feeling the first flutters of movement, often called 'quickening,' around this time!
17.mom_tip: Those flutters are real! It's bonding time.

18.description: Your baby's unique fingerprints and toe prints are now forming. Their nervous system is also maturing rapidly, allowing for more coordinated movements.
18.mom_tip: Dizziness can happen; stand up slowly.

19.description: A waxy, protective coating called vernix caseosa is beginning to form on your baby's skin. This coating protects them from the amniotic fluid.
19.mom_tip: Leg cramps? Stretching calves before bed helps.

20.description: Congratulations, you're halfway there! The 20-week anatomy scan is often performed around this time. It's a great opportunity to discuss your baby's growth with your doctor.
20.mom_tip: Halfway mark! Time to schedule that anatomy scan.

21.description: Your baby is regularly swallowing amniotic fluid, which is great practice for their digestive system. You're likely feeling their kicks and jabs more consistently now.
21.mom_tip: Varicose veins may appear; elevate your legs when possible.

22.description: Your baby now looks like a miniature newborn. Their senses of sight and hearing are continuing to improve, and they can even perceive your touch through the uterine wall.
22.mom_tip: Talk to your baby—they can hear you now!

23.description: Your baby's hearing is getting much better. They can now hear your heartbeat, your voice, and other sounds from outside. This is a perfect time to talk and sing to them!
23.mom_tip: Braxton Hicks contractions might start—stay hydrated.

24.description: A major milestone in lung development is happening this week as the branches of the respiratory 'tree' and surfactant production begin, making viability outside the womb a possibility.
24.mom_tip: Glucose screening test is usually coming up soon.

25.description: Your baby is getting plumper as they gain more fat, which is making their skin less translucent. They may even be able to respond to your voice with movement.
25.mom_tip: Restless legs? Try a warm bath and magnesium.

26.description: At 26 weeks, your baby's eyes are starting to open and they are becoming more sensitive to sound. It's a good time to discuss the upcoming glucose screening test with your doctor.
26.mom_tip: Swelling? Reduce salt and keep feet up.

27.description: You've reached the end of the second trimester! Your baby is practicing breathing by inhaling and exhaling amniotic fluid, and they may even have a regular sleep-wake cycle.
27.mom_tip: Second trimester is ending; prepare for the final stretch.

28.description: Welcome to the third trimester, the home stretch! Your baby's brain is developing rapidly, and they can now experience REM sleep, which means they might be dreaming.
28.mom_tip: Welcome to the 3rd Trimester! Count those kicks.

29.description: Your baby is demanding a lot of nutrients, especially calcium for their hardening bones. This is a great time to focus on calcium-rich foods to support their growth.
29.mom_tip: Baby needs calcium; yogurt or leafy greens are great.

30.description: Your baby is growing fast and gaining about half a pound a week from here on out. Their eyesight is continuing to develop, though their vision is still quite blurry.
30.mom_tip: Heartburn is common; try smaller, frequent meals.

31.description: All five of your baby's senses are now fully functional. They are busy processing information from all the sights, sounds, and tastes they are experiencing.
31.mom_tip: Shortness of breath happens as baby pushes up; sit tall.

32.description: Your baby is likely getting into the head-down position in preparation for birth. Their skin is becoming soft and smooth as they continue to plump up.
32.mom_tip: Practice pelvic tilts to ease back pressure.

33.description: Your baby's bones are hardening, but their skull remains soft and flexible. This allows the plates to overlap slightly, which helps them fit through the birth canal.
33.mom_tip: Waddling is normal; your pelvis is widening.

34.description: Your baby's lungs are nearly fully developed, and the protective vernix caseosa coating on their skin is getting thicker. They are getting ready for their big debut!
34.mom_tip: Hospital bag packed yet? Good time to start.

35.description: It's getting a bit crowded in there! Your baby doesn't have as much room to do somersaults, but you'll still feel plenty of strong kicks, jabs, and stretches.
35.mom_tip: Frequent urination returns; baby is sitting low.

36.description: Your baby may 'drop' into your pelvis around this time, a process called lightening or engagement. Be sure to discuss the signs of labor with your healthcare provider.
36.mom_tip: Breathing might get easier as baby drops.

37.description: Congratulations, you've reached full term! This means your baby is developed enough to be born at any time from this week forward. Their lungs are mature and ready for the outside world.
37.mom_tip: You are full term! Rest whenever you can.

38.description: Your baby is continuing to build a layer of fat to help them regulate their body temperature after birth. They are also shedding most of the fine lanugo hair that covered their body.
38.mom_tip: Look for the mucus plug; labor could be soon.

39.description: Your baby's brain is still developing at an incredible pace. It's one of the last organs to finish maturing, so every extra day inside helps them prepare for life outside.
39.mom_tip: Contractions? Time them. 5-1-1 rule is standard.

40.description: You've reached your official due date! While this is the day everyone focuses on, remember that many babies arrive a little earlier or later. Don't worry if they're taking their time.
40.mom_tip: Happy Due Date! Relax, baby comes when ready.

default.description: While I don't have a specific update for this week, development is happening every day! It's always best to discuss your baby's specific progress with your healthcare provider.
default.mom_tip: Listen to your body and rest when needed.

menstruation.description: Your cycle has begun. It's a great time to focus on rest, gentle movement, and nourishing foods.
menstruation.proactive_greeting: Cycle Day 1-5. It's perfectly okay to cancel plans and rest.

follicular.description: As your energy returns after your period, you might find it's a great time for more active workouts.
follicular.proactive_greeting: Your energy is building! Great time to tackle creative projects.

ovulation.description: You might be feeling a peak in your energy and mood around now. This is the fertile window of your cycle.
ovulation.proactive_greeting: You're at peak energy today! Social vibes are high.

luteal.description: As your body prepares for your next period, you might notice PMS symptoms. Gentle exercise and mindfulness can be very helpful now.
luteal.proactive_greeting: Nesting mode might be kicking in. Be gentle with yourself.

0-4_weeks.title: Newborn (0–28 days)
0-4_weeks.feeding: Only breastmilk (colostrum → mature milk). 8–12 feeds/24 hrs, 10–20 min each side.
0-4_weeks.weight_gain: Loses 7–10% in first week → regains birth weight by day 10–14.
0-4_weeks.poop_pee: Day 1–2: Meconium. Day 3–4: 6–8 wet diapers + 3–4 yellow stools daily.
0-4_weeks.milestones: Reflexes only (rooting, sucking, Moro). Brief alert periods, tracks light/red objects.
0-4_weeks.red_flags: Jaundice after day 4, no wet diaper >8 hrs, fever >38°C.
vaccinations: Hepatitis B birth dose (within 24 hrs, latest by 2 weeks)
0-4_weeks.mom_recovery: Focus on healing. Bleeding (Lochia) is normal. Sleep when baby sleeps is a cliché but true.
0-4_weeks.proactive_greeting: Welcome to the newborn bubble! ❤️ Remember, feeding 8-12 times a day is normal right now. Have you checked for 6+ wet diapers today?

1-3_months.title: Infant (1–3 months)
1-3_months.sleep: 15–17 hrs total. First stretches of 4–5 hrs at night start around 6–10 weeks.
1-3_months.milestones: Social smile (5–8 weeks), lifts head 45° when on tummy, coos, follows moving objects 180°.
1-3_months.new_things: 6-week growth spurt, peak fussiness at 6–7 weeks (PURPLE crying period).
1-3_months.red_flags: No smile by 8 weeks, poor head control, not calming with feeding/rocking.
1-3_months.mom_recovery: You might be cleared for gentle exercise at 6 weeks. Watch for postpartum hair loss (Telogen Effluvium) - it's temporary!
1-3_months.proactive_greeting: Baby is getting stronger! Have you seen that first social smile yet? Also, don't forget the 6-week vaccination appointment.

4-6_months.title: Infant (4–6 months)
4-6_months.feeding: Exclusive breastmilk/formula. Some doctors start dal water/rice water at 6 months (new IAP advisory).
4-6_months.sleep: 14–15 hrs. 4-month sleep regression common. Many do 6–8 hr stretch at night.
4-6_months.milestones: Rolls over both ways, laughs out loud, reaches & grabs toys, bears weight on legs, raking grasp.
4-6_months.new_things: Drooling & hand chewing starts (early teething in some).
4-6_months.red_flags: Not reaching for objects, stiff legs/crossed legs.
4-6_months.mom_recovery: Your sleep might get disrupted again by the 4-month regression. This is a survival phase, not a failure.
4-6_months.proactive_greeting: If sleep has gone haywire, blame the 4-month regression! 😴 Also, is baby trying to roll over yet?

6_months.title: Half-Birthday Milestone
6_months.feeding: First complementary food! Most Indian families start mashed rice/dal or ragi porridge. Continue milk.
6_months.mom_recovery: As baby starts solids, your breastfeeding rhythm might change. Stay hydrated.
6_months.proactive_greeting: Happy half-birthday! 🎂 Is today the big day for starting solids? Mashed dal or rice is a great first step.

7-9_months.title: Crawler (7–9 months)
7-9_months.feeding: 3 solid meals + breastmilk/formula. Finger foods, sippy cup introduction.
7-9_months.sleep: 13–14 hrs. 8–10 month sleep regression very common. Usually 2 naps.
7-9_months.milestones: Sits without support, crawls/commando crawls, pincer grasp, waves bye-bye, says 'mama/dada' (non-specific).
7-9_months.new_things: Stranger anxiety + separation anxiety peaks. Teething pain common.
vaccinations: 9 months: MMR-1 (or MR) + JE-1 (in endemic states)
7-9_months.red_flags: Not sitting by 9 months, no babbling, not transferring toys hand-to-hand.
7-9_months.mom_recovery: Back pain is common from lifting a heavier baby. Watch your posture.
7-9_months.proactive_greeting: Separation anxiety peaking? It's a sign of healthy attachment! 💜 Also, don't forget the MMR vaccine due at 9 months.

10-12_months.title: Cruiser (10–12 months)
10-12_months.feeding: 3 meals + 2 snacks + milk. Family foods mashed/chopped.
10-12_months.sleep: 13–14 hrs. 1–2 naps. Many stand and cruise.
10-12_months.milestones: Pulls to stand, cruises, may take first steps, says 1–3 clear words, points, follows simple commands.
vaccinations: 12 months: PCV booster, Hepatitis A-1 (some brands need 2 doses)
10-12_months.red_flags: Not pointing to objects, losing skills they had before.
10-12_months.mom_recovery: You made it to one year! It's time to schedule your own annual health check-up too.
10-12_months.proactive_greeting: Almost one! 🎈 Is baby cruising or standing yet? It's a great time to baby-proof those sharp corners.

13-15_months.title: Toddler (13–15 months)
13-15_months.feeding: Almost full family food (soft). Whole cow milk can start.
13-15_months.sleep: 12–14 hrs. Moving to 1 nap (many still on 2 naps).
13-15_months.milestones: Walks independently, climbs stairs with help, 4–10 words, stacks 2 blocks.
vaccinations: 15 months: MMR-2 (or MR + Measles), Varicella-1, PCV booster, Hepatitis A-2 (if needed)
13-15_months.mom_recovery: Chasing a walker is a workout! Ensure you are wearing comfortable footwear at home.
13-15_months.proactive_greeting: Welcome to the toddler years! 🏃‍♀️ Walking yet? Also, brace yourself—tantrums are a normal part of this new independence.

16-18_months.title: Toddler (16–18 months)
16-18_months.feeding: Eats with family, uses spoon (messy), drinks from open glass.
16-18_months.milestones: Runs, kicks ball, 10–50 words, points to 4–6 body parts, removes socks/shoes.
16-18_months.new_things: Potty training interest in some kids.
vaccinations: 16–18 months: DPT booster-1, IPV booster, Hib booster (if Pentavalent was used)
16-18_months.mom_recovery: Mental load increases as they get more active. Take 5 minutes for yourself today.
16-18_months.proactive_greeting: Is your little one running around now? 🌪️ It's also time for the DPT and IPV boosters if you haven't done them yet.

19-24_months.title: Toddler (19–24 months)
19-24_months.feeding: Eats everything family eats (mild spices ok).
19-24_months.sleep: 11–13 hrs + 1 nap (many drop nap around 2–2.5 yrs).
19-24_months.milestones: Jumps, speaks 50+ words & 2-word sentences, undresses self, parallel play.
vaccinations: 18–24 months: Typhoid conjugate vaccine (TCV), Hepatitis A, Varicella-2, DPT booster-2 (at 2 yrs)
19-24_months.big_milestone: Turns 2 years – annual health check + vision/hearing screening.
19-24_months.mom_recovery: Two years of parenting! Celebrate your resilience. 💪
19-24_months.proactive_greeting: Two-word sentences often start now! 'Mama, up!' 🗣️ Don't forget the Typhoid and Hepatitis A vaccines due in this window.
